samples.summary: clampPosToModel swallows an unresolvable blockId, but the very next call (anchorDocPosition) rethrows it uncaught from updateCursorPos
samples.evidence: clampPosToModel (l.957-977, touched by this delta) wraps everything in try/catch and returns `pos` unchanged when the block cannot be resolved — resolveBlockTreePath throws `Block not found: ${blockId}` (l.867). updateCursorPos then immediately calls `this.anchorDocPosition(clampedPos, clampedPos.lineAffinity)` (l.2999) with that same unresolvable position, and anchorDocPosition has no try/catch and no `if (!block)` guard: l.925 resolveBlockTreePath throws, or if it does resolve, `getBlockByRegion` (typed `Block` but can return `undefined` at runtime, l.1383-1394) feeds `this.blockTextLength(block)` at l.928 → TypeError. anchorDocRange (l.994) has the same exposure for selection endpoints. So the defensive catch added in clampPosToModel is illusory: a caret referencing a block a remote peer just deleted still throws out of updateCursorPos, which is called from the editor's cursor-move path with no caller-side handling.

samples.summary: activeCursorPos.lineAffinity is now published on the wire but the peer caret renderer hardcodes 'backward', so a peer's caret and their own highlight can render on different visual lines
samples.evidence: users.ts now types and the store publishes `activeCursorPos.lineAffinity`, yet editor.ts:1561-1568 calls `resolvePositionPixel(peer.position, 'backward', ...)` with a literal, and docs-view.tsx:226 forwards the position untouched. The affinity that is now transmitted is discarded, so at a wrap boundary a peer caret sits at the end of the previous line while the peer's selection rects (computeSelectionRects, which does honour endpoint affinity) sit on the next line. The users.ts comment acknowledges this, so it may be deliberate, but the information is available and unused.

samples.summary: Design doc statement contradicted by this delta: it claims activeCursorPos is not typed for lineAffinity, which users.ts now does
samples.evidence: docs-presence.md:190-194 states "The peer *caret* still resolves `'backward'`: `activeCursorPos` is not typed for the field". This delta adds `lineAffinity?: 'forward' | 'backward'` to `DocsPresence.activeCursorPos` (packages/frontend/src/types/users.ts:27), so the stated reason for the backward-only peer caret is now false and the doc misdescribes the wire shape.

samples.summary: Comment justifies the spread by citing deepStrictEqual, but the integration test it points at uses assert.deepEqual

finding.summary: clampPosToModel swallows an unresolvable blockId, but the very next call (anchorDocPosition) rethrows it uncaught from updateCursorPos
finding.evidence: clampPosToModel (l.957-977, touched by this delta) wraps everything in try/catch and returns `pos` unchanged when the block cannot be resolved — resolveBlockTreePath throws `Block not found: ${blockId}` (l.867). updateCursorPos then immediately calls `this.anchorDocPosition(clampedPos, clampedPos.lineAffinity)` (l.2999) with that same unresolvable position, and anchorDocPosition has no try/catch and no `if (!block)` guard: l.925 resolveBlockTreePath throws, or if it does resolve, `getBlockByRegion` (typed `Block` but can return `undefined` at runtime, l.1383-1394) feeds `this.blockTextLength(block)` at l.928 → TypeError. anchorDocRange (l.994) has the same exposure for selection endpoints. So the defensive catch added in clampPosToModel is illusory: a caret referencing a block a remote peer just deleted still throws out of updateCursorPos, which is called from the editor's cursor-move path with no caller-side handling.

verdict.reason: Every claimed element checks out. clampPosToModel (yorkie-doc-store.ts:957-977) swallows an unresolvable blockId via try/catch plus `if (!block) return pos`, returning the position unchanged; updateCursorPos then passes that same position straight into anchorDocPosition at :2999 and, for selections, anchorDocRange at :3001 (which forwards both endpoints to anchorDocPosition at :999/:1002). anchorDocPosition (:916-941) has no try/catch and no null guard: :925 calls resolveBlockTreePath, which throws `Block not found: ${blockId}` at :867, and :928 calls blockTextLength(block) (:912-914 does block.inlines.reduce) on the result of getBlockByRegion, which is declared to return `Block` but actually returns `blocks[topIndex]` (:1393) and can be undefined at runtime for a stale index — a TypeError. So the newly documented defensive catch protects only the presence payload, not the anchor computation two lines later. The path is real: updateCursorPos is called with no caller-side handling from docs-view.tsx:399 and from a throttled trailing setTimeout at docs-view.tsx:405-409 that replays a *captured* pos/sel later, precisely the window in which a remote peer's block deletion invalidates the blockId; publishResolvedLocalCursor (:2883) is a second unguarded entry. The editor's listener fan-out fireCursorMoveCallbacks (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1185-1194) iterates callbacks with no error isolation, so the throw also aborts later listeners and scheduleSpellRecheck(). I found no guard, validation, or catch anywhere on these paths that would make the throw unreachable, and unhandled-exception / missing-null-guard on a live cursor-move path is in the Correctness lane at major-or-worse impact.
